3. Petite fourmi de feu (PFF)
Log Little Fire Ant (Wasmannia auropunctata) survey points — pick a status, tap the map to add a point (add as many as you like, e.g. for a whole transect), then submit them all at once. They show up on "2. Map" (layer "Little Fire Ant (PFF)") and in "4. Chart analysis" for everyone within seconds.
Zone and Status here are just the default applied to new points — optional, and each point below can be given its own instead (edit it directly in the pending list). Status must be set (globally or per point) before submitting; Zone can be left blank.
Points — tap/click the map to add one (you can add several). Small dim dots already on the map are previously submitted PFF points (tap one for details); your new points stand out with a bold white outline:
Tap/click the map to add a point — you can add several before submitting.
From a handheld GPS (e.g. Garmin GPSMAP 65). "Import GPX file" reads one file you pick by hand. "Import from connected GPS" (Chrome/Edge desktop only) reads straight off the device once you grant access to its top-level folder — it searches every subfolder automatically for any .gpx file, so it works whatever folder structure your GPS uses. Each point's on-device color/icon sets its status automatically, learned once per symbol and shared with the whole team (see below the first time a new one shows up). Track logs aren't supported, only individually saved waypoints. Already-submitted points (same day, within ~20m) are skipped automatically, so re-importing is safe.

4. Invasive Bird Survey (point count)
Standardised 10-minute point count (50 m radius) for Common Myna (Acridotheres tristis) and Red-vented Bulbul (Pycnonotus cafer). Always use the same Station ID and return to the exact same GPS point every visit. Protocol: Papehue pilot study — native-canopy (Type A/A*) vs invasive-canopy (Type C) comparison. Data feed the habitat–invasive bird interaction analysis (Spotswood et al. 2013; Blanvillain et al. 2020).
Station & Session

Rows for Myna/Bulbul/Wattled 🔒 are auto-filled to match the Seen/Heard counts entered above — change those counts to add/remove rows. For each auto-filled row, set the distance, behaviour and height stratum for that individual. Behaviour F = foraging on Spathodea (flowers/fruit) is the key variable linking canopy type to bird use. Use "+ Add contact" only for another species observed opportunistically (e.g. Pomarea, or anything else).

Edit Management Unit — historical data (Butaud survey)

The first columns here come from the embedded Butaud historical survey (August 2023 / August 2024 / December 2025). One row per management unit, including any new zone drawn via "Add Elements" (shown here with blank fields — fill them in and Save the same way), or added manually below. "Dominance" normally auto-detects native vs. invasive vs. anthropic from the vegetation text (a heuristic word-parse) — set it explicitly here to correct a wrong call without having to reword the vegetation text. Use "+ Add column" to add an extra SB/Plantation/Vegetation session for a later date (2026, 2027, ...) — pick the real date of that session, not just a year: for every zone, whichever dated entry is genuinely the most recent (a fixed 2023/2024/2025 column or any dynamic column) becomes that zone's official value everywhere — the map layers, the τ-check tool, the combined historical+NRDS estimate, and the priority-zone rankings all pick it up automatically, per zone. Edits are shared with everyone using the app, not just this device. "Zone (Nom)" and "Valley" are the lookup keys used everywhere else and can't be renamed here; deleting a row only removes its historical data — a drawn polygon for that zone, if any, is kept.
No unsaved changes

4. Chart analysis

Choose an analysis above.

Repeat-visit pairs — empirical τ check

Diagnostic for the recency-decay τ used in the Combined Cleaning Estimate (τ_Miconia / τ_Spathodea, editable in the "Combined current estimate" calc box on the map). Two independent methods, shown and pooled separately (never averaged together): (1) from logged cleaning % — NRDS's Postgres column for this field was dropped entirely on 2026-08-25 (not just excluded going forward), so this method can no longer produce any new pairs, only whatever was already captured before that date. (2) from hours worked — for every repeat cutting/maintenance visit to the same zone, the next visit's hours (real, logged since 2026-08-25, or a 6h/person estimate for older sessions, marked *), converted to a %-of-zone-area via the same person-hours/ha rate used elsewhere in the app, stand in for how much regrew back since the previous visit. Pairs are grouped by the zone's dominant invasive genus (same field used everywhere else). This only counts and reports what the data currently supports — it does not automatically change τ.

Priority zones to work on

Three independent rankings for deciding which zones to work on next — planting, cutting, and maintenance — never blended into one number.

Last planting actions

Every PLANTATION action recorded, filterable by valley and zone, with a per-zone summary.

Last cleaning actions

Every CUTTING/MAINTENANCE action recorded, filterable by valley and zone, with a per-zone summary.

🧹✨ Last rat line cleaning

Rat-line cleaning is logged separately from zone-level cleaning actions (a per-line YES/NO "Cleaned" flag).

Cutting & Maintenance vs Plantation — compared

Invasive removal/control (CUTTING + MAINTENANCE, in person-hours) versus new planting (PLANTATION, in individuals) — two different kinds of field work, compared side by side rather than blended into one number.

Dératisation activity

Per-line summary — every rat-patrol line, its last check date and how long it's been since, sorted most-overdue-first by default. "Last avg Conso" blends per-station Checks and whole-line Conso_Ligne readings the same way the patrol history below does.

Patrol history

Every dératisation patrol with at least one recorded reading (per-station Checks or a whole-line Conso_Ligne), most recent first.
